label: Level 1 spells tier list, [Updated] part 2 (Grease to Wrathful Smite)

items.verdict: large concentration-free prone AoE using your save DC; held back only by being flammable
decent 4d6 plus advantage on the next attack, but Toll the Dead took over cleric filler damage
a bonus action and a spell slot for 1d10 in a tiny radius on a bad save
ranged bonus-action revive, and the delivery system for Whispering Promise and Hellrider's Pride buffs
bad damage ratio, but free action economy; retaliation builds and BUGS (works while raging, eats multi-hit spells) redeem it
5 temp HP per turn plus fear immunity, but needs long fights and no other temp HP source; he admits it is a pet spell
d6 on every attack roll all day, reapplied free on kills; enormous on multi-attack casters
the ranger's Hex; weapon attacks only, but the damage matches your weapon type
slightly more damage than cold Chromatic Orb with an ice surface; the pick for druids, who lack Chromatic Orb
highest single-target level 1 damage, effectively a cleric smite, but melee range is risky
free all-day +10 movement on everyone including summons; he would put it in S+ if that existed
+3 AC all day for unarmoured casters; useless early, near-mandatory once you want robes
cannot miss, ignores line of sight, splits across targets, and every flat rider applies per missile
disadvantage for aberrations and undead plus BROKEN TOOLTIP (real effect is blanket Frightened immunity, no charm protection); costs concentration
small poison damage on the worst save, with a weak and unreliable debuff attached
bonus-action untargetability; protects healers, haste concentration holders and low-health allies, and blocks doorways
less damage than plain Divine Smite and slower; worst of the smite spells, free only for Zariel tieflings
reaction +5 AC that only prompts when it turns a hit into a miss; worth a class dip on its own
+2 AC with no armour restriction, but costs concentration; best on one-level cleric dips
no-save disable that can end early encounters, then falls off a cliff past level three
real benefit, but the game hands out so many potions that taking the spell is redundant
weak early because damage grants extra saves; late, a 10-turn disable that bypasses boss incapacitation immunities
no concentration; 2d6 plus prone and knockback breaks caster concentration, and stacks with Divine Smite
panic-button push for cliffs and hazards, but a CON save and awkward 17-foot square limit it
useless normally; carried entirely by one upcast Tempest Cleric wet-crit build doing 300+ guaranteed damage
1d6 plus two turns of Frightened on a WIS save; now also a Hexblade spell after Patch 8

unassigned.why: counterfactual attached to Grease's A verdict — "it would be S tier if it wasn't flammable"
Heroism deliberation — "I was kind of tempted to give it B tier" — not the final letter
Heroism aside about other people's ratings — "a lot of people would have it in D tier"
restatement of Heroism's C verdict after the deliberation
closing remark about the series — expects "fewer and fewer S tier spells" at higher spell levels; rates nothing
